newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Telecom under renewed selling pressure.
newsitem.headline: Telecom under renewed selling pressure.

text.p: Telecom Corp of New Zealand, suffering the effects of lower brokers' earnings forecasts and a credit rating downgrade, was sold down again on Monday, continuing a trend that started in late January.
By 11.40 a.m. (2240 GMT) Telecom was down 13 cents (1.88 percent) at NZ$6.78 after renewed selling pressure through brokers JB Were, who have been active over the last three weeks.
As the midsession approached, Telecom was staging a partial comeback, trading up to NZ$6.84.

Tim Koller at Merrill Lynch said it didn't take long for Telecom to adjust down, having closed 11 cents weaker on Friday at NZ$6.91 and then trading at the equivalent of NZ$6.85 in the U.S., where its ADRs are listed.
"Telecom has just continued to weaken and there is still a good supply of stock there," he said.
Analysts said Telecom, which reports on Tuesday, is expected to come in with a net profit close to last year's of NZ$182.2 million.
The result was likely to include losses from its Australian unit, Pacific Star, which Telecom is in the process of selling.
Over the last month, Telecom has fallen from a high of NZ$7.58. At today's low, it has fallen 80 cents or almost 12 percent.
Over the course of this year, Telecom plans a NZ$1 billion share buyback, prompting ratings agency Standard and Poor's to downrade its long-term credit rating to AA from AA plus.

"This rating action follows TCNZ's decision to externally finance a NZ$1 billion share repurchase programme, continued downward pressure on margins, and uncertainty over TCNZ's multi-media investments," S&P said last Friday.
"People are taking a view that with a buy-back in play in the near future, that this is the opportunity for one or two of the big people to exit some stock," Nigel Scott at BZW said.
"That seems to be the market view, but it seems to have become self fulfilling" Scott said.
Telecom is just under half owned jointly by Bell Atlantic and Ameritech.
